title: RT and the Globe and Mail Wrote the Same Gaza Collapse Story
subtitle: Both held Israeli bombing structurally responsible for ceasefire-era deaths
body_md:
A war-damaged residential building in Gaza City collapsed on September 16, killing at least 21 people including six children, with dozens more trapped under rubble. The corpus covering this event is dominated by Global South and state-aligned outlets; Western Anglophone press — US and UK — is entirely absent. What the corpus shows is an unexpected convergence between its two most editorially opposed voices.

[RT](https://www.rt.com/news/645877-gaza-building-collapse-deaths/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=RSS) ran: "At least 21 people have been killed and dozens are missing after a bombed building collapsed in Gaza City." [Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-gaza-building-collapse-death-toll/) ran: "War-damaged Gaza building collapses killing 21 as perilous conditions persist during truce." Russia's state propaganda channel and Canada's centre-establishment broadsheet both characterised the collapse as a direct consequence of Israeli bombing during a ceasefire or truce period. The framing holds Israeli military action structurally responsible for post-ceasefire civilian deaths. Neither outlet qualifies this causal claim.

The single fullest account of what the collapse represents came from [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/world/mid-east/gaza-rescuers-recover-12-more-bodies-from-rubble-total-hits-75) (Turkey), whose full-body coverage disclosed the scale of Gaza's ongoing recovery backlog: 147 destroyed homes are being searched under a Civil Defense recovery project, approximately 1,072 people are believed buried beneath them, and 9,500 Palestinians have been reported missing since the war began. These numbers appear in no other outlet in this corpus. Without them, the story reads as a single incident during a truce. With them, it reads as one data point in a humanitarian backlog that makes post-ceasefire Gaza a zone of deferred, accumulating death long after active fighting paused. [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/world/mid-east/20-killed-when-building-damaged-in-israels-war-on-gaza-collapses) also reported: "The recovery effort has been slowed by severe shortages of heavy machinery and other equipment needed to clear the vast quantities of rubble."

Beyond the collapse itself, three outlets extended the frame in distinct directions. [CGTN Politics](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-09-15/21-Palestinians-injured-as-Israeli-strikes-continue-in-Gaza-1Qs3nEy6VSo/p.html?UTM_Source=cgtn&UTM_Medium=rss&UTM_Campaign=Politics) moved from the building to the institution: "strikes continued despite a ceasefire, with Gaza's already devastated education system facing further collapse." The only outlet to treat this as systemic institutional breakdown rather than a single physical structure. [Folha de São Paulo](https://redir.folha.com.br/redir/online/mundo/rss091/*https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/mundo/2026/09/predio-desaba-em-gaza-e-mata-ao-menos-20-ministro-de-israel-ameaca-retomar-guerra-e-expulsar-palestinos.shtml) was the only outlet to link the building collapse directly to an Israeli minister's threat to resume war and expel Palestinians, connecting an infrastructure incident to live ceasefire-politics. Iran's [Tehran Times](https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/530114/My-whole-family-is-either-dead-or-injured) led with survivor testimony as a headline: "My whole family is either dead or injured" — the only outlet to personalise the death toll through direct first-person voice.

[AfricaNews](http://www.africanews.com/2026/09/16/at-least-12-dead-and-dozens-missing-after-building-collapse-in-gaza-city/) filed the earliest and most conservative count — at least 12 dead — reflecting the gap between early reports from Shifa Hospital and later confirmed figures. [Egypt Independent](https://www.egyptindependent.com/gaza-building-collapse-kills-more-than-20-dozens-remain-trapped-under-rubble/) reported "more than 20 people, including several children." The Tehran Times and Daily Sabah both confirmed 21, including specifically six children.

The two most notable absences are structural. No US outlet appears in this corpus — American press likely covered Gaza from a ceasefire-negotiation or Israeli government perspective rather than foregrounding Palestinian casualty counts from building collapses. No Israeli outlet appears either, despite IDF war-damage legacy being directly implicated. The story of accumulated structural death in Gaza during a ceasefire is being covered primarily by Global South, state-aligned, and Turkish press — exactly those outlets whose credibility on this subject Western audiences are most conditioned to discount.
